newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ Alliance prepared to support minority coalition.
newsitem.headline: NZ Alliance prepared to support minority coalition.

text.p: New Zealand's left-wing Alliance Party said on Wednesday it would offer support to a Labour-New Zealand First minority government provided that it offered a programme that would advance the Alliance's key goals.

"While the Alliance would not join a coalition government, we are prepared to support a minority government with a programme which makes substantial progress towards our policy objectives," leader Jim Anderton said.

The Alliance, in a policy paper which has been presented to Labour leader Helen Clark, said it saw no reason why discussions should not start immediately and end well before December 13, the date by which parliament is due to reconvene.
It said a majority of New Zealanders had voted in Saturday's inconclusive general election for Labour, New Zealand First and the Alliance against the National Party government.

"The issues for discussion focus around the areas that the public put emphasis on during the election, including health, education, superannuation, the environment and foreign investment," Anderton said.
"If there are issues that the other parties believe should be put on the table for discussion, then the Alliance is ready to examine them."
The Alliance named its negotiating team as leader Jim Anderton, deputy leaders Sandra Lee and Jeanette Fitzsimons and national director Matt McCarten.

The Alliance paper draws comparisons between its own policies and those of Labour and NZ First. The paper shows similarities on health policy, mental health, accident compensation and education, although the amounts pledged by each party often differed.

It also found common ground on environment policy and pension policy, with all three parties favouring abolition of the superannuation surcharge and asset testing for long-term residential care for the elderly.
The three were also close in opposing state asset sales.

It pointed out differences in housing policy where NZ First wants to freeze state-house rentals rather than move from market to income-related levels, the latter being favoured by Alliance and Labour.

Under economic policy, the Alliance called for: "a commitment that the role of government is to provide balanced economic management, simultaneously seeking goals of full employment, environmentally sustainable development, price stability, social justice and balance of payments stability".
The sole reference to the Reserve Bank Act said the Alliance wanted to widen the central bank's goals "so as to prevent the systematic over-valuation of the dollar".
It also wanted to discuss the need for the government to maintain a balanced budget or small fiscal surplus over the economic cycle as a whole.
The Alliance cited New Zealand's balance of payments deficit as a particular concern and said it wanted to discuss specific actions to reduce it to prudent levels long-term.

"The Alliance has an economic policy package which addresses these issues, but we are prepared to negotiate over the specifics, provided the party or parties wishing to form a government propose viable and acceptable alternatives," it said.
